title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 17-24): Grothendieck is building finite combinatorial models ('maquettes') of one-dimensional tame ('modéré') spaces. A finite totally ordered set I with extremities ω0 < ω1 encodes a subdivided closed segment (I,∂I). The set M(I,∂I) contains the 0-cells, the points a ∈ I, and the 'intervals' I_{a,b} (a<b), seen as open 1-cells or segments. It carries relations ◁ (incidence / being in the closure), ≤ (order), ≪ (strictly to the left of) and ∥ (disjointness or incomparability). Constructible portions (Σ_con) that are mutually commensurable reduce to Boolean operations in some P(Φ_T) (previous page).

Case (2) treats a segment where one or both extremities are not given. One views it as a 'residual' or 'complementary' piece of the closed case, with one or both endpoints removed.

On this page, removing ω0 gives Omb°({I_{ω0,ω1}, ω1}) = M∖ω0, i.e. M with the point ω0 deleted. Topologically this is the half-open segment (0,1]. Its combinatorial counterpart is the pair (J, ω1), where J = I∖{ω0} is a finite chain with greatest element ω1. The objects of M(J,ω1) are:
- the points a ∈ J;
- the finite intervals J_{a,b}, a<b in J;
- the 'traces' J_{<a} of the former intervals I_{ω0,a}. These are now intervals open and unbounded on the left, and a may even be maximal.

The relations ◁, ≤, ≪, ∥ on M(J,ω1) = M(I,∂I∖{ω0}) can therefore be written intrinsically in terms of (J, ω1), without reference to (I,∂I).

Degenerate example: I = {ω0,ω1} gives J = {ω1} and M(J,ω1) = {ω1, J_{<ω1}}, a two-element maquette. On the next page he notes that |J_{<ω1}|° = ∅ (no interior vertices) while the cell J°_{<ω1} itself is nonempty. Next he treats the symmetric case (remove ω1, use J_{>a}) and the open case (remove both endpoints, use J_{<a}, J_{>a} and a unit object [J]).

Purpose: to get intrinsic combinatorial descriptions of the three non-compact variants of the subdivided interval (half-open on either side, open). These are the building blocks of a combinatorial or tame theory of 1-dimensional stratified spaces.
errors: No mathematical error. The only subtlety is that J_{<a} must be allowed for maximal a (a = ω1) and for the minimal element of J, giving 'intervals' with no interior vertices. Grothendieck flags this himself in the marginal note and on the next page (|J_{<ω1}|° = ∅ but J°_{<ω1} ≠ ∅).

ideas.what: Combinatorial model of a subdivided segment as a poset of vertices and open edges with incidence/order relations
ideas.modern_name: face poset of a 1-dimensional regular cell complex / stratified interval; combinatorial models in tame (o-minimal) topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (combinatorial topology); o-minimal cell decomposition: van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn (1980s)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is only sketched programmatically in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this specific combinatorics is unpublished

ideas.what: Half-open and open intervals obtained by deleting endpoints, encoded intrinsically by a chain with a greatest element (or least, or neither) plus 'unbounded' cells J_{<a}, J_{>a} and a unit cell [J]
ideas.modern_name: non-compact stratified 1-manifolds with boundary; open-cell/link combinatorics; cf. exit-path categories of stratified intervals
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; stratified-space combinatorics: Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2010s) in a different setting

deep.surprise_reason: The page is careful but elementary bookkeeping: the combinatorial description of half-open intervals by deleting an endpoint of a finite chain. It is of interest only as part of Grothendieck's unpublished 1986 program on combinatorial 'maquettes' for tame topology. It contains no new result or connection by itself.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: the struck-out word before Omb° is 'Mais' (crossed out), consistent with the transcription.
'(partie de M formée par ω0)' should read as M deprived of ω0 (complement of ω0). The word after 'formée' is unclear in the image, but the formula M∖ω0 makes the meaning clear.
Marginal note: '(on ne suppose plus ici que a ne soit pas maximal, cf. plus bas)'. It is positioned next to J_{<a}.
Line after 'plus précisément, la': the word read as 'sous-catégorie' is doubtful; it may be 'sous-maquette' or 'sous-ensemble'.
